verses.zh: 耶和华如此说：你们当守公平，行公义；因我的救恩临近，我的公义将要显现。
verses.en: This is what the Lord says,“Promote[NOTE:1] justice! Do what is right!For I am ready to deliver you;I am ready to vindicate you openly.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “guard”; KJV “Keep”; NAB “Observe”; NASB “Preserve”; NIV, NRSV “Maintain.”
Heb “for near is my deliverance to enter, and my vindication [or “righteousness”] to be revealed.”
verses.commentary:
56:1 This chapter starts out with two commands related to an appropriate life of faith (cf. Isa. 55:7).

- preserve justice ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 1036, KB 1581, cf. Isa. 1:17);
for "justice," see

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGE, JUDGMENT, JUSTICE

- do righteousness ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 793, KB 889);
for "righteousness," see

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ The reason for the life of faith is

- My salvation is about to come ‒ Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 97, KB 112,
cf. Isa. 46:13; 51:5; Ps. 85:9)

- My righteousness to be revealed ‒ Niphal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT
(BDB 162, KB 191, see same first two references as #1)

NT Believers must live every day as if the Lord was returning! This attitude and
lifestyle keeps us close to God (cf. Ps. 85:9), as it did the faithful followers under the Old Covenant (i.e. Ps. 1).

verses.zh: 谨守安息日而不干犯，禁止己手而不作恶；如此行、如此持守的人便为有福。
verses.en: The people who do this will be blessed,[NOTE:1] the people who commit themselves to obedience,[NOTE:2] who observe the Sabbath and do not defile it,who refrain from doing anything that is wrong.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “blessed is the man who does this.”
Heb “the son of mankind who takes hold of it.”
Heb and who keeps his hand from doing any evil.”
verses.commentary:
56:2 Notice the first two lines are parallel. Also the "blessed man" (cf. Ps. 1:1-3; 112:1; 119:1-2; 128:1)
is the one who obeys/observes God's law.

▣ The second two lines describe two specific things that "the blessed man" will not do.

- keeps from profaning the sabbath (cf. Exod. 20:8-11; 31:16-17; 35:2-3; Isa. 58:13; see SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH)

- keeps his hand from doing any evil (summary phrase)

The VERB "keep" (BDB 1036, KB 1581) occurs four times in this chapter
(Isa. 56:2 [twice],4,6). Lifestyle faith and obedience are vital and crucial aspects of a personal relationship
with YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

verses.zh: 与耶和华联合的外邦人不要说：耶和华必定将我从他民中分别出来。太监也不要说：我是枯树。
verses.en: No foreigner who becomes a follower of[NOTE:1] the Lord should say,‘The Lord will certainly[NOTE:2] exclude me from his people.’The eunuch should not say,‘Look, I am like a dried-up tree.’”
notes: Heb “who attaches himself to.”
The infinitive absolute precedes the finite verb for emphasis.
verses.commentary:
56:3 This verse assures those who were normally excluded from Israel's God that they would be included.

- the physically damaged person (cf. Isa. 56:6-8, Deut. 23:1-8)

- the non-Israelite worshiper (cf. Isa. 56:4-5)

The word "says," which is repeated twice (foreigner, eunuch) is a Qal IMPERFECT
(BDB 55, KB 65) used in a JUSSIVE sense.

▣ "surely separate" This is a Hiphil INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and a Hiphil
IMPERFECT from the same root (BDB 95, KB 110) used for emphasis. However, the great
emphasis is that this statement is not true!

▣ "the eunuch" This refers to a person

- with damaged testicles

- a castrated person

- a royal servant (i.e. Potiphar and Daniel)

The account of the Ethiopian eunuch in Acts 8 being fully accepted into the people of God
by faith in Jesus Christ, the Suffering Servant, is a great example of this type of persons' inclusion!

verses.zh: 因为耶和华如此说：那些谨守我的安息日，拣选我所喜悦的事，持守我约的太监，
verses.en: For this is what the Lord says:“For the eunuchs who observe my Sabbathsand choose what pleases meand are faithful to[NOTE:1] my covenant,
notes: Heb “and take hold of” (so KJV); NASB “hold fast.”
verses.commentary:
56:4 Notice the qualifications of a faithful eunuch.

- keeps My sabbaths ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERFECT

- chooses what pleases Me ‒ BDB 103, KB 119, Qal PERFECT with waw

- holds fast My covenant ‒ BDB 304, KB 302, Hiphil ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

verses.zh: 我必使他们在我殿中，在我墙内，有记念，有名号，比有儿女的更美。我必赐他们永远的名，不能剪除。
verses.en: I will set up within my temple and my walls a monument[NOTE:1] that will be better than sons and daughters.I will set up a permanent monument[NOTE:2] for them that will remain.
notes: Heb “a hand and a name.” For other examples where יָד (yad) refers to a monument, see HALOT 388 s.v.
Heb “name” (so KJV, NIV, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
56:5 Eunuchs could have no natural children (i.e. "a dry tree," v. 3) so YHWH will give the faithful eunuchs a memorial
in His house (i.e. temple). He will give them "an everlasting name" (i.e. Hebrew idiom for descendants).

verses.zh: 还有那些与耶和华联合的外邦人，要事奉他，要爱耶和华的名，要作他的仆人―就是凡守安息日不干犯，又持守他（原文是我）约的人。
verses.en: As for foreigners who become followers of[NOTE:1] the Lord and serve him,who love the name of the Lord and want to be his servants—all who observe the Sabbath and do not defile it,and who are faithful to[NOTE:2] my covenant—
notes: Heb “who attach themselves to.”
Heb “and take hold of”; NAB “hold to”; NIV, NRSV “hold fast.”
verses.commentary:
56:6 Notice how the faithful foreigners are characterized.

- join themselves to the Lord ‒ Niphal PARTICIPLE (BDB 530, KB 522)

- minister to Him ‒ Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 1058, KB 1661)

- love the name of the Lord ‒ Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 12, KB 17;
see SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH)

- be His servants ‒ Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 224, KB 243)

- keep from profaning the sabbath ‒ Qal PARTICIPLE (BDB 1036, KB 1581, cf. vv 2,4)
and a Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 320, KB 319)

- holds fast My covenant ‒ Hiphil PARTICIPLE (BDB 304, KB 302)

YHWH's true followers are known by their lifestyle faith (cf. Matthew 5-7, esp.
Matt. 7:15-23,24-27; Eph. 1:4; 2:10; James 2:14-26).

verses.zh: 我必领他们到我的圣山，使他们在祷告我的殿中喜乐。他们的燔祭和平安祭，在我坛上必蒙悦纳，因我的殿必称为万民祷告的殿。
verses.en: I will bring them to my holy mountain;I will make them happy in the temple where people pray to me.[NOTE:1] Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on my altar,for my temple will be known as a temple where all nations may pray.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in the house of my prayer.”
Heb “for my house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations.”
verses.commentary:
56:7-8 As Isa. 56:6 described the faithful foreigners' actions, so Isa. 56:7-8 describe what
the faithful God will do for them.

- I will bring to My holy mountain (i.e. temple, cf. Isa. 27:13; 57:13; 65:14; 66:20; Jer. 31:23; Ezek. 20:40; Dan. 9:16,20)

- I will make them joyful in My house of prayer

- I will accept their sacrifices on My altar

- I will gather them and others

56:7 "My house will be called a house of prayer for all the peoples" This was the stated purpose
of Solomon's temple (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:41-43,60). Jesus quotes this verse in Matt. 21:13; Mark 11:17; Luke 19:46
as He cleansed Herod's temple (i.e. the court of the Gentiles) of the animal sellers and money changers. For a complete listing of this
universal element in Isaiah see Isa. 45:22.

▣ "burnt offering" See SPECIAL TOPIC: BURNT OFFERING.

verses.zh: 主耶和华，就是招聚以色列被赶散的，说：在这被招聚的人以外，我还要招聚别人归并他们。
verses.en: The Sovereign Lord says this,the one who gathers the dispersed of Israel:“I will still gather them up.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The meaning of the statement is unclear. The text reads literally, “Still I will gather upon him to his gathered ones.” Perhaps the preposition ל (lamed) before “gathered ones” introduces the object of the verb, as in Jer 49:5. The third masculine singular suffix on both עָלָיו (ʿalayv) and נִקְבָּצָיו (niqbatsayv) probably refers to “Israel.” In this case one can translate literally, “Still I will gather to him his gathered ones.”
verses.commentary:
56:8

NASB
"Yet others I will gather to them"

NKJV
"Yet I will gather to him others besides"

NRSV, Peshitta
"I will gather others to them"

(Peshitta, "to him")

TEV
"has promised that he will bring still

other people to join them"

NJB
"there are others I shall gather"

JPSOA
"I will gather still more to those gathered"

REB
"I shall add to those who have already

been gathered"

LXX
"I will gather to him a congregation"

There are two possibilities.

- YHWH will gather even more of the exiled descendants of Abraham (JPSOA, LXX, NET, cf. Isa. 60:4-14)

- YHWH will gather other outcasts (i.e. foreigners, eunuchs, cf. Isa. 19:24-25; 60:3; 66:18-21; Joel 2:28-32)

Jesus' use of this text in Mark 11:17, following the LXX, shows its wider intended scope;
also note John 10:16. This is the thrust of Joel 2:28-32 (quoted by Paul in Rom. 10:13).

verses.zh: 田野的诸兽都来吞吃吧！林中的诸兽也要如此。
verses.en: All you wild animals in the fields, come and devour,all you wild animals in the forest!
verses.commentary:
56:9 This is a parody of the invitation to the Divine supper (cf. Isa. 56:12; 55:1-2), but here in
the context of judgment (Isa. 56:10-12) it is a command ("come" ‒ BDB 87, KB 102, Qal
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT). This will be a banquet of judgment!

There is an interpretive question related to Isa. 56:9-12, as to when this occurs.

- pre-exilic

- exilic

- post-exilic

The issue is to which period of Israel's history do these verses refer? Possibly it relates
to some in each period (i.e. multiple fulfillment prophecy, or at least the historical ambiguity of Isaiah's poems can
relate to different periods). There were always faithless leaders and people.

verses.zh: 他看守的人是瞎眼的，都没有知识，都是哑巴狗，不能叫唤；但知做梦，躺卧，贪睡，
verses.en: All their watchmen[NOTE:1] are blind,they are unaware.[NOTE:2] All of them are like mute dogs,unable to bark.They pant,[NOTE:3] lie down,and love to snooze.
notes: The “watchmen” are probably spiritual leaders, most likely prophets and priests, responsible for giving the people moral direction.
Heb “they do not know”; KJV “they are all ignorant”; NIV “they all lack knowledge.”

The Hebrew text has הֹזִים (hozim), which appears to be derived from an otherwise unattested verbal root הָזָה (hazah). On the basis of alleged cognates, BDB 223 s.v. הָזָה offers the definition “dream, rave” while HALOT 243 s.v. הזה lists “pant.” In this case the dog metaphor of the preceding lines continues. The reference to dogs at the beginning of v. 11 favors the extension of the metaphor. The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa has חזים (“seers”) here. In this case the “watchmen” are directly identified as prophets and depicted as lazy.
verses.commentary:
56:10-12 These verses are in sharp contrast to the faithful outcasts of Isa. 56:1-8. These describe
Israel's spiritual condition (mostly her leaders).

- the watchmen (spiritual leaders) are blind

- all of them know nothing

- all of them are dumb dogs

- dream/rave

- from Arabic root or "pant" (KB 243), referring to "dogs" of Isa. 56:10c

- DSS has "seers," referring to prophets

- love to sleep

- greedy

- never satisfied

- shepherds without understanding

- all tuned to their own ways (cf. Isa. 53:6)

- each one turned to unjust gain

- drunkards

- no plans or motive to change their evil ways

Wow! What a terrible description of the covenant people. Their leaders are corrupt and
the proverb is true, like leader, like people! God's revelation, temple, and godly leaders had made
no difference (i.e. Roim. 9:4-5). Their fruit is obvious (i.e. self)!

56:10 "His watchmen are blind" The MT scholars noted a problem in the Hebrew text. It reads
a Qal PERFECT (BDB 859, KB 1044), but they suggest a Qal PARTICIPLE.
Either one does not change the sense of the text.

verses.zh: 这些狗贪食，不知饱足。这些牧人不能明白―各人偏行己路，各从各方求自己的利益。
verses.en: The dogs have big appetites;they are never full.[NOTE:1] They are shepherds who have no understanding;they all go their own way,each one looking for monetary gain.[NOTE:2]
notes: The phrase never full alludes to the greed of the leaders.
Heb “for his gain from his end.”

verses.zh: 他们说：来吧！我去拿酒，我们饱饮浓酒；明日必和今日一样，就是宴乐无量极大之日。
verses.en: Each one says,[NOTE:1] “Come on, I’ll get some wine!Let’s guzzle some beer!Tomorrow will be just like today!We’ll have everything we want!”[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “each one says” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “great, [in] abundance, very much,” i.e., “very great indeed.” See HALOT 452 s.v. יֶתֶר.
verses.commentary:
56:12 "Come" This IMPERATIVE (Qal, BDB 87, KB 102) matches the one
in Isa. 56:9c! The humans come to get drunk and ignore God (Isa. 56:12b), so now the animals are invited
by God to come and devour His covenant people (cf. Isa. 18:6; Jer. 7:33; 12:9; 15:3; 34:20).

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

There is a change from Isaiah's message to the returnees from Mesopotamian exile
(Isaiah 40-55) to the faithless, covenant people in Palestine (Isaiah 56-66).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 56:1-5

1Thus says the Lord,

"Preserve justice and do righteousness,

For My salvation is about to come

And My righteousness to be revealed.

2How blessed is the man who does this,

And the son of man who takes hold of it;

Who keeps from profaning the sabbath,

And keeps his hand from doing any evil."

3Let not the foreigner who has joined himself to the Lord say,

"The Lord will surely separate me from His people."

Nor let the eunuch say, "Behold, I am a dry tree."

4For thus says the Lord,

"To the eunuchs who keep My sabbaths,

And choose what pleases Me,

And hold fast My covenant,

And a name better than that of sons and daughters;

I will give them an everlasting name which will not be cut off."
